rulings.question_as_you_read_it: May a Qere (read form) be written with the source's morpheme separator stripped, and may a read form occurring nowhere in the running text be presented as a quotation?
rulings.ruling: (1) A Qere MAY be presented, and never as running text: it is labelled as the read form from the note layer (the corpus already does this — '(oshb:Ezek.16.13, Qere)' — and the toolkit's QERE tier already sanctions it when a K/Q keyword stands within 160 characters). A read form presented without that label is a defect. (2) The morpheme separator '/' is OSHB morphology markup, not text; the running-text extract itself drops it by convention (TOOLKIT: 'No … morpheme /'), so a Qere rendered WITHOUT the slash is the correct rendering and one rendered WITH it would be presenting markup as text. Every read form in the corpus is already slash-free. (3) A written form (ketiv) is quoted as the unpointed running-text bytes. (4) Naming a variant site instead of rendering it remains permitted and preferred where nothing turns on the form. (5) TOOLING, not rows: pmarks kq entries concatenate ketiv and qere with no delimiter (e.g. the 1:8 entry is ketiv then qere run together); the extraction should carry ketiv and qere as separate fields with the separator preserved in a morphology field (method §13 item 2). This ruling governs Ezekiel and is proposed for the method (§17 loop) as the campaign-wide answer to §13 item 3; cross-generation reconciliation with M9 (§1) is the orchestrator's duty and is not done here.

rulings.question_as_you_read_it: How far does T4-03 ('a denial placed behind a comma reads RED and is a rewording order, never a pass') reach beyond dateline and puncta claims, does a coordinate chain of denials trigger it, and what severity band does it carry when the denied fact is true?
rulings.ruling: SCOPE: the rule reaches every absence claim about a checkable layer (mark, K/Q, paseq, puncta, dateline, editorial note, formula device) that is APPENDED behind a comma to a clause whose head is a different claim, or set off parenthetically inside a positive claim (P07-008's 'held, then not resolved' shape). Its rationale is machine-checkability: the toolkit's checkers cannot bind a denial that sits outside its clause. A COORDINATE CHAIN consisting solely of absence claims over one named span ('no K/Q note, no paseq, no parashah mark and no editorial note lie within this span') is NOT a hidden denial: each item shares the verb and the scope and the checker's absence-phrase arm reads it; it PASSES. BAND: LOW when every denied fact is true and no boundary rests on the denial (form only); MEDIUM when a denied fact is false or the denial carries the seam; never HIGH on form alone.
